metadata.title: Palantir's 30% Surge Just Crushed the Short Trade

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR, Financials), the artificial intelligence and military software business, jumped over 30% Tuesday, leaving investors betting against the stock with roughly $3 billion in paper losses.Data from S3 Partners shows the move wiped all of the short sellers year-to-date gains in Palantir.Short sellers borrow shares to sell, with the hope of buying them back at a lower price later. When a stock goes up , those positions lose value and may be compelled to close . This adds more buying pressure .Palantirs surge followed quarterly earnings that above Wall Streets expectations and a better full-year outlook. Strong growth in the companys U.S. commercial and government divisions helped boost investor confidence in demand for its artificial intelligence platform.The losses underscore the risk of shorting a stock with significant momentum and a loyal retail-investor base. But the surge has also boosted Palantirs valuation, boosting pressure on management to maintain its present pace of development.And short posture is crowded and might help underpin future increases if negative investors keep covering their bets, but could also add to the volatility.Then investors will want to know whether Palantirs revenue growth can support the stocks value after results.
